newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end higher, boosted by strong Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end higher, boosted by strong Dow.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed sharply higher as investors refused to take profits and followed Wall Street's bullish mood, traders said.
The Bovespa index of 49 most-active stocks closed up 2.6 percent at 9419. Volume was strong at 688 million reais ($655 million). Nearly half was in Telebras shares.
The Dow was up 57 points at the Bovespa close, giving investors added reason to support local shares, traders said.
"We thought we would see some profit-taking today, but the market kept going. There was active buying at home and from abroad," said one trader.
There was no local news to explain the rise in individual share prices, traders said. Telebras preferred shares shares gaining 3.37 percent at 108.75.
Telebras preferred on Monday closed 40.4 percent higher year to date, outperforming the Bovespa's 37 percent rise since January 1, traders said.

The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) powered 1.77 percent ahead to close at 2641. The index, which includes the nine most liquid power stocks, was driven upward by gains in state-owned power company Eletrobras.
Eletrobras preferred shares rose 3.06 percent to close at 505.

Despite strong gains Monday, many players said a long overdue bout of profit-taking was in order. They noted that some investors could use tomorrow's February trade balance, expected to come in $1.6 billion in the red, as an excuse to sell off.
